answer:
Your Porto weekend note now has a trip page. You'll find it under **Page** in the note.

- **Countdown:** it counts down to Fri 16 Oct, so 11 days to go today.
- **At a glance:** both flights, the hotel (address, confirmation number, check-in time) and the ~6000 kr budget.
- **Ideas and to-dos:** each is a tickable list with a progress bar. Ticking an item on the page updates the note.

I made small changes to the note so the page could read it. The ideas are now `- [ ]` checklist items under an "Ideas" heading, and "To do before" has a heading too. I split the flights into "Flight out" and "Flight back" lines. I also added a colon after "Budget". The wording is otherwise the same.

  "guide": "# Building Amber Notes pages

A page turns a note into a small app: a habit grid, a budget with totals, flashcards, a reading log. The note's markdown is the data and stays the source of truth: the person can always flip to Text and see and edit every row. The page is a view and a remote control for that data. Deleting or replacing a page never loses data.
